He also posits that because of how aircrafts crash, those aircrafts have historically been more dangerous than they would have been otherwise.
Of course, another issue surrounds the airlines' global presence because they collect disparate information on crash risk.

He explains that health problems are not as straightforward as they appear.
As a simple study example, he asks if an aircraft has mechanical failure, does that mean it has pollution on the airplane? I suppose it cryptically asks if mechanical shop worker pollution on the airplane is distinct from spray from pollution/top control valve.

On the other hand, he does point out that one doesn't always know if it's the mechanical system or human factors.
